objective: Bind strict external evaluation to a canonical public provider/model/runner system identity in addition to exact source identity.
actions: Implemented a canonical secret-free public runtime/system manifest and validator.
Bound the manifest SHA-256 into the strict external evaluation request subject.
Required the runtime-manifest binding again inside the production external-claim bridge so legacy source-only requests fail closed.
Extended exact-commit handoff generation to emit source artifact, public system manifest, and strict request together.
Added tamper, secret-field, runtime-change, source/runtime consistency, claim-gate, and CLI regression tests.
Merged only after exact-head full CI success.
observations: PR 150 fixed tracked-source identity but did not distinguish different provider/model/runner configurations sharing that source.
PR 152 closes request-level runtime reassignment, while actual runtime use and evaluator independence still require independently signed production evidence.
claims: Strict external evaluation requests now cryptographically commit to a public runtime/system manifest digest as well as exact tracked source.
This is evaluation-subject hardening, not evidence that the declared runtime was used or that AGI was achieved.
